page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2a server family. It is powered by a single dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 physical core based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This configuration does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the single-core architecture delivers average results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests with a score of 1783.48, but falls into the lower percentiles for multi-core and memory-intensive operations. The memory subsystem recorded a read-only small block bandwidth of 70.86 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 7.95 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, the instance achieved 1.27 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 1.38 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is aided by hardware-accelerated AES support, though the processor lacks advanced vector or matrix extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, utilizing dedicated physical resources rather than shared-core burstable models. However, the single-core limitation and lower memory bandwidth restrict its utility for parallel processing or heavy data-science tasks. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and simple utility services that do not require high multi-threaded throughput or local storage.
